rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO David Risher executed THREE open-market code-P purchases during the drawdown: (1) 2025-09-03: 5,926 sh @ $16.875 = $99,996; (2) 2025-12-10: 5,030 sh @ $19.8046 = $99,617; (3) 2026-02-13: 7,490 sh @ $13.375 = $100,179. Total $299,792 of personal cash, all open-market code P, in disciplined ~$100K monthly cadence. Crucially, share count INCREASED as price FELL ($19.80 -> $16.88 -> $13.38), i.e., Risher scaled INTO weakness rather than backing off. Feb 13 buy was THREE days after the FY2025 10-K filing (Feb 11) at the lowest price of the three. Risher holds 11.48M shares post-trade — meaningful personal stake (~0.6% of basic shares outstanding). NO other officer/director executed open-market purchases. The pattern is consistent with a self-imposed monthly buying program, but the SEC code is unambiguously P (open-market) not A (grant) — these are at-risk dollars.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest single positive signal in the file. CEO putting personal cash to work in a disciplined cadence that ACCELERATED (shares purchased rose) as price dropped is the textbook honest-insider alignment signal. The dollar size is modest in absolute terms ($300K) but it is the cleanest possible Form-4 evidence: open-market P-code, by the CEO, with size scaling INTO drawdown, AND clustered AFTER earnings disclosures (not before). Combined with continued $1.75B buyback program execution, this directly contradicts a 'liar/distress' narrative the -43% drawdown would imply.

rfm_tuples.f: Aggregate dollar value of open-market sales (code S) vs purchases (code P) across all reporting insiders since 2025-08-01. Cross-reference each S transaction date against the 8-K calendar to test for pre-bad-news clustering.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Open-market SALES (code S) total $6,202,332 across 6 insiders over 10 months. Largest: Director Prashant Aggarwal $3,892,886 on 2025-12-03/04 @ ~$22.30 (rule 10b5-1 plan exit per earlier Forms 3/4 footnote pattern). Next: SVP Lindsay Catherine Llewellyn $1,411,091; CFO Erin Brewer $487,230 (Aug-Sept 2025 only, NO sales in 2026); Chief Accounting Officer Stephen Hope $180,120; Director David Lawee $148,322; Director Jill Beggs $82,682. P:S dollar ratio = 0.048 (i.e., sales exceed buys 20:1 in $$). HOWEVER: timing analysis is important — (a) Aggarwal $3.9M block on 2025-12-03/04 was 28 days AFTER Q3 2025 earnings 8-K (2025-11-05, beat with $46M net income) at the local price peak $22.30, BEFORE the Feb 2026 drawdown; (b) Brewer's sales were Aug 20, Sept 3 2025 at $15-18, BEFORE the major drawdown (price still in mid-teens range); (c) NO CFO/CAO/CEO open-market sales in 2026 at all; (d) the 2026-02-24, 03-03, 04-21, 05-22 Form 4s by CFO Brewer, CAO Hope, SVP Llewellyn are predominantly code F (RSU tax withholding) and code A (RSU vesting grants), NOT discretionary sales. Llewellyn's two 2026 code-S transactions ($354K Feb 25 + $355K Apr 17) are visible but small.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mixed picture. Headline dollar P:S of 0.048 is poor and would be a SHORT-tier signal in isolation. But two mitigators: (1) the largest seller is a director on a 10b5-1 program selling at the LOCAL HIGH ($22.30) — that's a feature of plan-based selling, not insider information; (2) C-suite open-market sales STOPPED in 2026 once the drawdown deepened, and the CEO STARTED buying — exactly the asymmetry we want. Net: moderately negative on raw insider dollars, but the qualitative ordering (CEO buying, CFO not selling) is positive and the timing is not pre-bad-news.

rfm_tuples.R: "Net income $2,844.0 million" (FY2025 vs $22.8M FY2024) — 124x YoY growth headline; "Diluted EPS $6.81."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification) — decompose the $2.8B net income to test whether it represents recurring operating earnings or one-time items. Compare GAAP vs adjusted measures and the tax line specifically.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K MD&A + Note on income taxes + reconciliation table)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Income before tax FY2025 = ($53.2M); BENEFIT FROM income taxes = +$2,897.3M. Net income = $2,844.0M. The benefit of $2.897B comes from RELEASE OF DEFERRED TAX ASSET VALUATION ALLOWANCE on U.S. federal and certain state deferred tax assets in Q4 2025 (issuer explicitly discloses: 'a $2.9 billion benefit from the release of our valuation allowance of U.S. federal and certain state deferred tax assets in the fourth quarter of 2025'). Underlying pre-tax operating loss was ($53M). Adjusted EBITDA $528.8M (+38% YoY); Free cash flow $1,115.6M (+46% YoY) is the cleaner cash measure. Without the valuation allowance release, GAAP net income would have been a small loss, NOT $2.8B.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. The $2.8B / $6.81 EPS headlines are tax-accounting-driven (an audit-required true-up reflecting management's confidence in future taxable income), NOT operating performance. Issuer DOES disclose the $2.9B item transparently in MD&A — this is not deceptive. But the disclosure could mislead retail readers anchored on EPS. The underlying business is profitable on adj-EBITDA and FCF basis but barely above breakeven on operating GAAP. Severity is MODERATE not SEVERE because (a) full transparency, (b) the val-allowance release itself is a forward-looking POSITIVE signal — auditors only allow this when future profitability is 'more likely than not.'

rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2025: Active Riders 29.2M (Q4 ending) vs 24.7M FY2024 (+18%); Rides 945.5M (+14%); Gross Bookings $18.507B (+15%); Adjusted EBITDA $528.8M (+38%); FCF $1.116B (+46%). Q1 2026: Active Riders 28.3M (+17% YoY, record Q1, 6th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth); Rides 236.9M; Gross Bookings $4.946B (+19%); Adj EBITDA $132.8M (+25%); FCF $287.3M; Net income $14.2M vs $2.6M. Issuer disclosed a slight definitional refinement to Active Riders calculation (no impact to prior periods per MD&A). All metrics improved YoY.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: KPIs are corroborated and trend is unambiguously positive. The growth INACCELERATED in Q1 2026 (Active Riders 17%, GB 19%, Adj EBITDA 25%). This is the central fundamental disconnect from the -43% drawdown: business operating metrics do not show the kind of deterioration that would justify the price action. Drawdown is sentiment-driven (Tesla robotaxi launch + Waymo + Uber competition), not fundamental.

rfm_tuples.R: "In February 2026, we authorized a new share repurchase program for the repurchase of up to $1.0 billion of the Company's Class A common stock, in addition to amounts remaining available under our existing repurchase program under which we were authorized to repurchase a total of $750 million."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the buyback authorization and execution against (a) cash position, (b) cap structure, (c) actual share count reduction.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 5 + Note 12 + Q1 2026 10-Q equity statement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: As of Dec 31 2025: $500M of $750M existing authorization already executed (incl. 5.7M sh @ ~$16.79 in Sept 2025 with 2030 Notes issuance). Feb 2026 added new $1.0B authorization ON TOP, for $1.25B total available. Q1 2026 weighted-average diluted share count = 402.5M vs 424.0M Q1 2025 (-5.1% YoY) — material share-count reduction. This is a high-conviction management posture, not a hedged 'in line' guide. If business is actually deteriorating, the guide is reckless; if business is sound, the drawdown is wrong. Combined with CEO buying, points hard to LONG-tier.

rfm_tuples.R: "In 2021, we sold our self-driving vehicle division... so we must develop and maintain partnerships with other companies to offer AV technology on our platform." Lists Waymo (Alphabet), Zoox (Amazon), Baidu, Bolt, Tesla as competitors.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the drawdown is most likely AV-driven (Tesla robotaxi, Waymo expansion), test issuer's AV strategy concreteness vs hand-waving.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Concrete (not hand-waving) AV positioning: (a) Nashville Flexdrive AV operation announced opening this fall 2026 using May Mobility partnership; (b) Mobileye partnership announced; (c) First Baidu vehicles secured in UK; (d) Q1 2026 press release: 'state-of-the-art Flexdrive AV operation in Nashville sets the stage for a hybrid AV future. Lyft is performing while transforming.' Risk factors do NOT include a going-concern, material weakness, or business-model-existential AV warning; the AV disclosure is in the standard 'highly competitive market' framing. No goodwill impairment of any segment. Flexdrive subsidiary provides actual vehicle inventory that could be AV-converted (asset advantage vs Uber asset-light).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The drawdown is plausibly AV-narrative driven. Lyft's response is multiple OEM/AV partnerships (May Mobility, Baidu, Mobileye) — which is the asset-light platform play. Management has converted Flexdrive from a rental fleet to a potential AV-ready fleet. Disclosure is consistent and concrete, but Lyft has NO captive AV technology (sold to Toyota Woven in 2021 for $550M) — this is a real long-tail risk if Waymo/Tesla execute pure-play robotaxi at scale. Issuer is honest about this dependency. The market may be pricing this terminal-value risk, but the near-term financials disprove an immediate impairment. Mode-B mild gap: 10-K could more explicitly quantify partner economics.

summary: LYFT is a -43.4% drawdown name where Form 4 forensic evidence directly and cleanly REJECTS the distress narrative. CEO David Risher executed three open-market code-P purchases ($99,996 + $99,617 + $100,179 = $299,792 total) on 2025-09-03, 2025-12-10, and 2026-02-13 — disciplined ~$100K monthly cadence in which share count INCREASED as price FELL ($19.80 -> $16.88 -> $13.38), i.e., scaling INTO weakness, all clustered AFTER earnings disclosures not before. Risher holds 11.48M shares (~0.6% basic SO). NO C-suite open-market sales in 2026 at all; CFO Brewer's only sales were Aug-Sept 2025 at $15-18 and STOPPED. The recent May 22 Form 4s (filed 3 days pre-cutoff) are all code F (RSU tax withholding) and one code G (gift to trust) — zero opportunistic selling at $13. Headline net income $2.844B is dominated by a $2.897B valuation allowance release (Mode B catch, transparently disclosed) — underlying GAAP pre-tax was ($53M) — but Adj EBITDA $528.8M (+38%), FCF $1.116B (+46%), and Active Riders 29.2M (+18%) are real. Q1 2026 accelerated: GB +19%, Active Riders +17%, Adj EBITDA +25%. Q2 2026 guide of GB +18-21% and Adj EBITDA $160-180M (margin EXPANSION) was issued 18 days before cutoff. Buyback authorization $1.75B (with $1.25B remaining), diluted share count -5.1% YoY, $1.8B unrestricted liquidity, PwC clean opinion, no going-concern, no material weakness. The -43% drawdown is sentiment-driven (AV-competitive narrative: Tesla robotaxi, Waymo) rather than fundamental — Lyft mitigates with May Mobility/Baidu/Mobileye AV partnerships and Flexdrive fleet. P:S dollar ratio 0.048 is the one moderate negative (selling exceeds buying 20:1 by $$), but the largest seller (Director Aggarwal $3.9M @ $22.30) was 10b5-1 plan-based at the LOCAL HIGH and pre-drawdown. Verdict: LONG-tier — clearest CEO-honest-insider setup in the universe alongside the strong KPI/guide acceleration. Severity: 6 PASS / 4 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED_FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE.
